newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Poland's PM says confident of NATO invitation.
newsitem.headline: Poland's PM says confident of NATO invitation.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said on Wednesday he was confident Poland would become a member of NATO although a special agreement between the alliance and Russia could weaken the position of new members.
NATO and Russia agreed a deal in Moscow on Wednesday after months of tough negotiations intended to sweep away Moscow's concerns over the expansion of the Western defence alliance.
Cimoszewicz, on an official visit to Sweden, was speaking to reporters before the deal was announced.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to receive the first invitations to join the 16-member alliance at a NATO summit in Madrid in July.

"The agreement will give Russia some special position in relation to NATO, guaranteeing not only involvement but also to have some influence, some input on what will go on in NATO," Cimoszewicz said, speaking in English.
"From that point of view Poland is interested in achieving at least the same status in the time of our negotiations with NATO," he said.
A new agreement between Russia and NATO could leave potential members like Poland without much say in the group, Cimoszewicz said.
"From my point of view it can be a kind a paradox that a country that is not going to join NATO, like Russia, may get a stronger position in relation to NATO than applicant countries," he said.
"But if it can be solved that our position is well understood by NATO member countries' partners, I think we can at least achieve the same position at the Madrid summit," he said.

In Warsaw, Poland's Fopreign Minister later formally welcomed Wednesday's deal between Russia and NATO, saying that work on the western military alliance's eastward expansion would now proceed in a better climate.
"Poland welcomes the agreement..., which is a basis for cooperation and lowering tensions in Europe," Dariusz Rosati told reporters.
Cimoszewicz said he was confident Poland would become a member of NATO sometime in the next two years and that, during the Madrid summit, NATO would invite some countries to negotiate membership.
"I am fully confident that Poland would be among those countries invited for negotiations," he said.
"Poland expects to have those membership negotiations this year, to finish them this year and to become a NATO member in the next two years," Cimoszewicz said.

Cimoszewicz was in Sweden for a two-day visit with Prime Minister Goran Persson to discuss topics including a pipeline network around the Baltic carrying North Sea gas to Poland and a joint project launched to combat organised crime.
